content.text:
I've submitted index 3 (Sb fraction 0.353) as the best composition. At 0.069%, it had the highest EQE of the five I measured.

| Index | Sb fraction | EQE (%) |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0.280 | 0.028 |
| **3** | **0.353** | **0.069** |
| 4 | 0.383 | 0.056 |
| 8 | 0.513 | 0.024 |
| 13 | 0.659 | 0.001 |

- **Where the peak is:** EQE rises from the most Pb-rich point, peaks around Sb 0.35–0.38, then falls to almost nothing by Sb 0.66. The lower-EQE points on both sides confirm this is a local maximum. The other untested points between them (indexes 1, 2, 5, 6, 7) could still be a little higher.
- **Last measurement:** a curve fit through my first three Pb-rich points put the peak near Sb 0.39. Index 4 (Sb 0.383) came in at 0.056%, just below index 3.
- **Ruled out:** the GP model suggested the Sb-rich end (indexes 24–28). I skipped it because EQE fell steadily from Sb 0.35 to 0.66. That suggestion rested only on uncertainty, since none of my measurements were in that region.
- **Still unmeasured:** the Sb-rich end (Sb 0.68–0.91), apart from how EQE dropped on the way there.
- **XRD not used:** all 5 XRD measurements were left unspent, so I haven't confirmed which crystal phases are present. The candidate structures are Pb₂Sb₂O₇ at Sb 0.5 and PbSb₂O₆ at Sb 0.667.
